Scope: road works, storm, sewer, potable water and TSE networks, electrical works, fence and gates, a bridge and landscaping. Contract value 86.8M SAR, 24 months.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. At 78.2% against a plan of 51.2%, the project is 27.0% ahead (SPI 1.53). This week it gained 1.27% against 1.11% planned, less than last week's 1.80%. The schedule now forecasts completion 140 days after the contract date, 33 days earlier than last week's forecast.

Well ahead on progress, but the forecast finish is still more than four months late. Both the weekly report and the P6 update forecast completion on 06-Apr-2028, 140 days after the contract completion date of 18-Nov-2027, with −120 days of total float (−148 last week). This is 33 days earlier than last week's forecast, the second gain in a row; the report does not say why. The other open milestones slipped again, 7 days each and 12 days for roads and medium voltage, the fifth weekly slip in a row. Roads and medium voltage, the WBS furthest behind plan (73.5% against 100%, unchanged for five weeks), depends on the MV network, which is waiting for the MODON–SEC agreement; MV cable, ring main units and lighting substations have not been ordered.

The two sources swap the dates of two milestones. The weekly report forecasts roads and medium voltage on 20-Feb-2027 and the deep network on 17-Jul-2027; the P6 export gives the same two dates the other way round. All other forecasts agree. Completion moved 33 days earlier, but the other open forecasts moved 7 days later than in the 10-Nov report (roads and medium voltage 12 days), so the approvals and purchase-order milestones (28-Nov and 22-Nov last week) are now due on 05-Dec and 29-Nov-2026.

Data notes

Built from the 17-Nov-2026 weekly upload (W08), with the 10-Nov-2026 upload (W07) for this week's changes.

  • Week number: the report states week 51.86 (whole weeks since site handover: 51); the file reference is WPR-052.
  • Physical progress differs between sheets: the dashboard shows 78.2% (559,019 of 714,561 man-hours), while the P6 export and the Physical-Chart Data sheet show 79.8% (570,508 man-hours).
  • The weekly summary file (works executed this week) and the Look Ahead and Conclusion sheets label cost-based progress as "actual"; this report uses physical % complete (man-hours) only. The weekly summary file also gives project code JDH3-03-011, contract value 86,742,345 and an expected finish of 30-Nov-2026, as does the Look Ahead sheet; the dashboard and P6 forecast 06-Apr-2028. The Look Ahead sheet still carries the 03-Nov schedule statistics (432 critical activities).
  • MODON PM: Eng. Abdallah Aljulayfi in the General Information sheet and the Risk & Issue Log; م. رضا المنشاوي in the Look Ahead sheet and the weekly summary file.
  • Milestones: P6 and the weekly report still swap the roads/MV and deep-network forecast dates, and the dashboard's "Original (Baseline)" column shows last week's forecasts (e.g. 09-May-2028 for project finish). The finish moved 33 days earlier while total float improved by 28 days (−148 to −120); the approvals and purchase-order milestones gained 28 days of float although their dates slipped 7 days. The report gives no reason.
  • Manpower: the November manual head count fell from 182 in last week's report to 117 and equipment from 75 to 47, so the month's figure is overwritten each week; the equipment plan is 56 in the summary and 57 in the breakdown, and cumulative equipment actual stays at 564 from July.
  • HSE inspection of 17-Nov-2026 repeats the results of the two previous weeks exactly (7 good, 13 need improvement, 3 failed, score 0.73). In the HSE audit log, the week-52 audit (16-Nov-2026) is closed on 13-Nov-2026, before it was issued (14-Nov-2026). In the quality audit log, the week-52 audit is closed on 18-Nov-2026, after the data date.
  • Quality: field inspection requests issued fell from 5,549 to 5,521, and approved road shop drawings from 335 to 267 while total road drawings stayed at 337.
  • Material Monitoring: paint on cement plaster shows 1,520 m² installed although none is recorded as delivered, and TSE HDPE pipe shows 8,772 m installed against 8,722 m delivered. Pavement markings are not delivered there but "Delivered Done" in the Procurement sheet. Installed kerbs and pavers jumped by 8,998.5 m and 9,264.8 m² in one week, to exactly 95% and 93% of their quantities, while the Major Quantities sheet shows no change.
  • The Procurement Log file is identical to last week's, unchanged for the fifth week running.
  • Invoice Log: the payment average duration shows −5,762.75 days and invoice 8's payment period −46,336 days, formula errors; the 36,000 deduction on invoice 8 still has no stated reason.
  • Risk & Issue Log (new file): its dashboard counts 246 open risks and 133 open issues, but every category total is 0 and each log holds a single entry (the MV agreement).
  • HDPE pipes: the plan-to-date entry error for the 8,722 m line is corrected (7,021 m); the sheet still does not name the network.
  • Several dashboard cells show #REF! errors.
